reason: The sources provide over 10 cross-verified claims across multiple distinct domains to support a high-impact 45-second narrative about Voyager 1's dormant thruster test.
story: In 1977, NASA launched Voyager 1 on an ambitious grand tour of the outer solar system. The spacecraft delivered historic flybys, discovering active volcanoes on Io and detailed ring structures around Saturn before pushing past the outer boundary of the heliosphere. In August 2012, Voyager 1 made history by becoming the first human-made object to cross into interstellar space. By 2017, after four decades traveling through deep space, its primary orientation thrusters were degrading. To keep the probe's antenna locked onto Earth, engineers attempted a daring test: firing a set of backup thrusters that had been completely dormant since 1980. Operating over 11 billion miles away, the 37-year-old backup thrusters fired perfectly, extending the operational lifetime of humanity's farthest interstellar scout.
angle: NASA successfully fired backup thrusters on Voyager 1 in 2017 after 37 years of total dormancy in interstellar space.

claims.claim: Voyager 1 was launched after its twin probe Voyager 2.
Voyager 1 traveled on a faster trajectory than Voyager 2 to reach its planetary targets sooner.
Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object from Earth.
Voyager 1 surpassed Pioneer 10 in 1998 to become the farthest human-made object.
Voyager 1 conducted flybys and detailed studies of Jupiter.
Voyager 1 discovered active volcanoes on Jupiter's moon Io.
Voyager 1 discovered two new moons around Jupiter, named Thebe and Metis.
Voyager 1 performed a flyby and detailed scientific observation of Saturn.
Voyager 1 found that Saturn's upper atmosphere consists of about seven percent helium, with almost all the rest being hydrogen.
Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in August 2012.
Engineers successfully fired backup thrusters on Voyager 1 in late 2017 that had been dormant since 1980.
Voyager 1 carries a Golden Record phonograph containing spoken greetings in 55 languages.
The Golden Record on Voyager 1 includes music by Chuck Berry.
Voyager 1 will remain within the bounds of the solar system until it emerges from the Oort Cloud in thousands of years.

disputed: Exact date of the 2017 thruster test: S1 states December 2017 while S2 specifies November 29, 2017. Script should attribute to late 2017.
Exact calendar day of entering interstellar space: S2 key dates list August 1, 2012, while S1 specifies August 25, 2012. Script should state August 2012.
Timeframe to exit the Oort Cloud: S1 estimates approximately 30,000 years to pass through, whereas S2 estimates 14,000 to 28,000 years. Script should describe it generally as thousands of years.
